The test image shows a mango leaf with scattered dark/black spots across the surface, yellowish-green discoloration, and what appears to be small dark lesions distributed across the blade. The spots are small, discrete, and somewhat irregular. No powdery coating visible. No tip dieback or browning from the tip. No sooty black coating covering large areas.

Key observations:
- Multiple small dark spots/lesions scattered across the leaf
- Yellowish-green background color (chlorosis)
- Spots appear as small dark puncture-like lesions

This pattern is consistent with Anthracnose (small dark necrotic spots) rather than Powdery Mildew (white powder), Die Back (tip browning/necrosis), or Sooty Mould (black sooty coating over large areas).

Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The Anthracnose reference shows a more advanced stage with large necrotic areas and browning. The test image has smaller, more scattered discrete dark spots on a green leaf — characteristic of earlier-stage Anthracnose. Sooty Mould would show a more continuous black coating; Powdery Mildew would have white powder; Die Back would show tip/margin browning.

The scattered small dark lesions on a yellowing green leaf align most closely with Anthracnose.
